items.text: Explore historical and contemporary elements of the social environment and personal identity.

Explore using Michif French for following protocol when welcoming visitors and Elders/Lii pleu vyeu (e.g., welcoming into a space, offering a gift or tobacco, pulling out a chair, offering tea, serving of food).

Explore using Michif French while completing routine tasks of the home and classroom (e.g., washing dishes, tidying the house/class, laundry, wiping the table, help to prepare a meal, setting the table).
Explore how routine tasks in the home and classroom have changed over time.
Investigate local historical and contemporary spaces, businesses or schools by reaching out to community members for information, stories, and support.
Investigate opportunities in Saskatchewan to participate in Michif French culture with the guidance of a Language Carrier or Lii pleu vyeu.
Begin to develop relationships by visiting with local community members, Language Carriers, Elders, collectives, clubs and local Métis organizations.

Apply, with support, a variety of before, during, and after comprehension strategies to construct meaning in Michif French written texts and oral communications, with the guidance of a Language Carrier or Lii pleu vyeu.
Learn through la manyair dis promnii (e.g., with Lii pleu vyeu, Language Carriers, family, peers or learning circles) both inside and outside of the classroom.

Review interpretation of written texts and oral communications, after reading and listening, using strategies such as:
• discussing key words in oral and written texts;
• making connections between new information, prior knowledge and personal experience; and,
• reacting with emotion (e.g., empathy, surprise, appreciation or dislike).

Begin to develop personal language learning tools (e.g., classroom/personal Michif French Dictionary, self-created pronunciation audio files) on topics such as home items, routines, hobbies and foods.

Consult resources (e.g., Lii pleu vyeu, Language Carriers, peers, family, Michif French dictionaries and mobile apps, anchor charts, websites) and visual aids (e.g., pictures, graphs and drawings) to help construct meaning of written texts and oral communications.
Apply, with support, a variety of strategies to produce Michif French written texts and oral communications.
Learn through la manyair dis promnii (e.g., with Lii pleu vyeu, Language Carriers, family, peers).
Explore how interactions with the land contribute to authentic Michif French language acquisition.
Explore the Michif French language for personal communication on topics, such as introductions, greetings, general interactions, phrases to participate in a discussion.
Use tools such as graphic organizers and outlines to make a plan for speaking or writing.

Consult resources (e.g., Lii pleu vyeu, Language Carriers, peers, family, Michif French dictionaries and mobile apps, anchor charts and websites) and visual aids (e.g., pictures, graphs and drawings) to support the production of oral and written texts.

Discuss how to take risks, try unfamiliar approaches, and experiment with various forms of expression (e.g., reduce anxiety by using mental techniques, such as positive self-talk and humour, to instill confidence).
Identify prior knowledge for personal expression in Michif French.
Describe physical (e.g., gestures and facial expressions) and auditory (e.g., laughter, tone, volume) cues to convey meaning.
Retell (in English) a Michif French oral communication with Lii pleu vyeu, Language Carriers, peers, or family members.
Demonstrate a short dialogue (e.g., practise, rehearse, role-play) with classmates in Michif French.
Reflect on personal strengths and needs with respect to one’s Michif French language and culture learning journey.
Determine personals strengths as a language learner.
Identify personal needs related to speaking, listening, reading, and writing in Michif French.
Recognize that risk-taking and a positive attitude are part of effective language learning.
Identify how la manyair dis promnii helps to meet personal language learning needs.
Celebrate personal Michif French language learning successes.

Reflect on identity through the Michif/Métis worldview and language by considering questions such as:
• How does la manyair dis promnii help to improve my understanding of the Michif French language and worldview?
• How does my use of Michif French shape the way I understand my social environments?
• How does my use of Michif French shape the way I understand my own identity?
• How does my use of Michif French shape the way I understand the Michif culture and community?
Identify, with support, when listening and reading, Michif French language concepts including basic context- specific vocabulary, word order and linguistic conventions.

Recognize context-specific and common vocabulary (e.g., lii zhours – days, lii mwaan – months, lii zoochii a likol – school supplies, paarchu dju korr – parts of the body, lii maanzhii - food, lii noombr - numbers).
Discuss the use of singular personal pronouns (e.g., Ji, Ja, Je, Tchu, Ta, y, il, ell).
Identify appropriate prepositions in context (e.g., annaryayr - behind, annavaan – in front of, dissu – on top of, ennhou - above, akoootii – beside, didaan – inside).
Recognize directional terms in context (e.g., dret - right, goosh - left, nor – north, sud – south, ouest - west, lest – east).
Recognize definite (e.g., le la, lay, lii) and indefinite articles (e.g., aen, de, day, dii).
Explain simple sentences in context (e.g., Netway la taab - Clean the table, Monnom ay – My name is, Je rest a – I live in, Jem sa maanzhii – I like to eat).
Identify, when speaking and writing, Michif French language concepts including basic context-specific vocabulary, word order and linguistic conventions.

Recognize context-specific and common vocabulary (e.g., lii zhours – days, lii mwaan – months, lii zoochii a likol – school supplies, paarchu dju korr – parts of the body, lii maanzhii - food, lii noombr - numbers).
Recognize the use of singular personal pronouns (e.g., Ji, Ja, Je, Tchu, Ta, y, il, ell).

Listen to or view a variety of simple oral Michif French communications (e.g., how to videos, storytelling videos, in-person visiting, songs) that address big ideas:
• elements of social environment;
• elements of personal identity; and,
• elements of Michif French culture.
Interpret simple oral communications or conversations.
Respond appropriately in structured interactions with common, simple, short phrases.
Respond to simple questions regarding personal identity (e.g., name, hometown, family names, interests, and hobbies).
Compare information related to others’ personal identity (e.g., name, hometown, family names, interests, and hobbies).
Describe personal reactions to simple oral communications with emotion (e.g., empathy, surprise, appreciation or dislike).
Construct meaning, with support, of a variety of simple written non-fiction and fiction Michif French texts on familiar topics.

Read a variety of simple written Michif French texts (e.g., children’s books, recipes, dictionaries, conversational sentences) that address elements of:
• the social environment;
• personal identity; and,
• Michif French culture.
Comprehend simple labels within the school in Michif French.
Repeat the basic directions of written imperative texts.
Respond to a survey regarding personal identity (e.g., name, hometown, family names, Treaty area, hobbies, age, preferred foods).
Identify the vocabulary words in context in written texts on familiar topics.
Discuss the possible variations within the written orthography of Michif French based on regional variation or language carrier preference.

Produce personal greetings (e.g., on the phone, in video recordings, in person).

Write about a variety of daily topics, such as personal details (e.g., name and age), dates (e.g., days of the week, months, seasons) and school/classroom items and routine.
Communicate simple written expressions (e.g., wii - yes, noo - no, sil voo play - please, maarsii –thank you, bonn mataen - good morning, boon apray mijii - good afternoon, Je regret - I’m sorry).
Compose a greeting card (e.g., Bonn Fayt- birthday, maarsii – thank you, Schwettchu vyen bayn - I hope you get well soon) using simple expressions.
Create simple social media posts using basic vocabulary (e.g., personal introduction, homeland).
Provide basic written directions to a place within the school or community using imperative sentences.
Experiment with communicating messages in a variety of written formats (e.g., notes, lists, paragraphs, graphs, emails, blogs and text messages).
Draft descriptions of personal lived experiences or activities related to the big ideas.

Explore historical and contemporary elements of the natural environment and kinship.
Recognize personal roles and responsibilities in family and community according to the Michif/Métis core values).
Discuss the traditional and contemporary roles of women in maintaining kinship ties and caring for each other.

Discuss places in Canada where Michif French is and was historically spoken (e.g., St. Laurent, St. Eustache and Saint Ambroise in Manitoba, the St. Louis Batoche, St. Laurent, the Duck Lake region in Saskatchewan, and the Lac la Biche, St. Paul, St. Albert and Bonnyville areas in Alberta).
Investigate opportunities in Saskatchewan to participate in Michif French language revitalization.

Discuss the transmission and endangerment of the Michif French language (e.g., Why was Michif French not always taught at home? Why were people reluctant to speak Michif French? Why and when did this stigma shift?).
Compare Michif languages (Northern, Heritage & Michif French) in terms of their origin, similarities, and differences.
Consider effective ways that local Indigenous language revitalization approaches have been implemented.
Discuss Indigenous language revitalization projects in other parts of the world and how successful strategies can be applied to Michif Language revitalization efforts in Saskatchewan.

Explore Michif language programs that exist (e.g., Michif Kindergarten, online classes, in-person classes, language nests, post-secondary classes, community-led Michif classes).
